item.title: Senate committee takes up nominees for NASA chief financial officer and inspector general
item.description: A Senate committee is set to advance nominations for NASA’s chief financial officer and inspector general.

item.title: China launches pathfinder spacecraft for “Origins” space science flagships
item.description: MANCHESTER, England — China launched a four-satellite technology demonstration mission Wednesday to test key instruments for upcoming flagship space science missions, including a lunar-orbiting radio array.

item.title: France awards $1.7 billion contract for next-generation spy satellites
item.description: JOHANNESBURG — France has awarded Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space a contract worth more than 1.5 billion euros ($1.7 billion) to develop two next-generation military Earth observation satellites.

item.title: Revolv Space closes $5.6 million Series A
item.description: WARSAW, Poland — Revolv Space, an aerospace power system developer based in Italy and the Netherlands, has closed a 5 million euro ($5.6 million) Series A round led by Deep Ocean Capital, aiming to use the funds to bolster research and development as well as production capacities. That brings the company’s fundraising total to 8.6 million euros, 7.8 million of which are in equity, Revolv Space said in a Nov. 11 fundraising announcement.

item.title: SpaceX to study options to bridge commercial and military satellite networks
item.description: The Space Development Agency awarded SpaceX a nearly $10 million contract to examines Plaser integration with missile-warning and tracking systems

item.title: China recruits international partners for 34-satellite cislunar constellation
item.description: MANCHESTER, England — China is recruiting international partners for a constellation of small spacecraft occupying nine-day elliptical orbits reaching lunar distance targeted for launch in 2030.

item.title: Horizon Microtechnologies Targets Constellation-Scale Production As Esa Phi-Lab Selection Strengthens Industrialisation Push
item.description: (Karlsruhe, Germany, September 29th 2026) Horizon Microtechnologies is accelerating industrialisation of its metallised polymer micro-additive manufacturing platform through IP-MASS, a two-year scale-up project supported by €500,000 and reinforced by selection […]

item.title: Firefly remains committed to Eclipse as it sells engines to AST SpaceMobile
item.description: Firefly Aerospace defended its agreement to sell rocket engines, rather than rocket launches, to AST SpaceMobile, calling it a “transformative deal” that gives it capital to accelerate its own vehicles.

item.title: Sierra Space gets FAA reentry license for Dream Chaser
item.description: Sierra Space is planning a first flight of its Dream Chaser spacecraft in the spring of 2027 after receiving a reentry license from the FAA.

item.title: Reflect Orbital raises $73.5 million
item.description: Reflect Orbital, a company whose plans to reflect sunlight to specific locations on the ground have attracted both interest and controversy, has raised $73.5 million.

item.title: AST SpaceMobile discloses role in Space Force airborne-tracking program
item.description: Direct-to-device satellite company expects $100 million from subcontract to STR for technologies for tracking airborne targets from orbit

item.title: Iridium pitches new satellite services as it awaits Pentagon contract renewal
item.description: As Rocket Lab acquisition moves forward, Iridium seeks to expand its military communications business with direct-to-device technology

item.title: AST SpaceMobile plots 40-50 satellites for Japanese direct-to-device network
item.description: AST SpaceMobile plans to build as many as 50 satellites for a joint venture with Japanese technology conglomerate Rakuten, which is in line for up to 148 billion yen ($1 billion) in subsidies to develop Japan’s own direct-to-device network by March 2029.

item.title: Anduril unveils satellite technology for space surveillance
item.description: The company says it’s demonstrated new playloads aboard its first integrated satellite, including an infrared sensor designed to track spacecraft in Earth's shadow.

item.title: Kratos and Seagate Space Partner to Advance Mobile Offshore Launch Capabilities for National Security Missions
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CA, November 10, 2026 – Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc., a technology company in defense, national security, and global markets, today announced a long-term agreement with Seagate […]

item.title: Enpulsion and Orbion collaborate on spacecraft propulsion systems
item.description: Two spacecraft propulsion companies are partnering to provide electric thruster systems for European spacecraft manufacturers.

item.title: Kuaizhou to debut reusable Kuaizhou-6 and low-cost Kuaizhou-12 rockets in 2027
item.description: MANCHESTER, England — Chinese launch firm Kuaizhou Aerospace plans to conduct first launches of new rockets next year, including a first-stage recovery attempt.

item.title: High demand prompts Rocket Lab to raise launch prices
item.description: Rocket Lab is increasing prices for launches of its Electron and Neutron rockets, citing high demand for the vehicles in a constrained market.

item.title: ESCAPADE on its way to Mars after Earth flybys
item.description: Two NASA smallsats are headed toward Mars after completing flybys of Earth nearly a year after their launch.

item.title: Rocket Lab gets Pentagon financing to boost Neutron production
item.description: A $150 million government loan would support production and recovery infrastructure for the reusable rocket

item.title: Firefly sees business opportunities as Pentagon turns to cislunar space
item.description: Space Force's emerging plans for military operations near the moon are drawing interest from spacecraft manufacturers and ground communications providers.

item.title: Globalstar approved to deploy next-gen direct-to-device constellation
item.description: France has cleared Globalstar to launch and operate the 54 next-generation direct-to-device satellites that the U.S.-based operator aims to begin deploying next year.

item.title: Planet books launches with Stoke Space
item.description: Earth observation company Planet announced a launch deal with Stoke Space as part of efforts to diversify access to space for its imaging spacecraft.

item.title: CCIA Report Highlights Satellite Connectivity’s Potential to Expand Internet Access and Drive Economic Growth
item.description: Washington — The Computer & Communications Industry Association today released Connecting the World: Unlocking the Potential of Satellite Connectivity, a new report examining how satellite technology can expand internet access, […]

item.title: White House declaration reaffirms freedom of American activities in space
item.description: A White House “declaration” about American freedom in space largely reaffirms existing policy and law, leading to reactions ranging from dismissal to cautious support.

item.title: Ceres-2 reaches orbit, Kinetica-2 lofts Qianfan satellites in four-launch week for China
item.description: MANCHESTER, United Kingdom — Second flights of the Ceres-2 and Kinetica-2 rockets marked commercial launch progress for China alongside further Long March launches for state programs.
